# QuaRot End-to-End 4-bit Quantization on LLaMA-2: Experiment Design (Design-Only)

Status: design-only study. No experimental run is performed in this phase; no numerical outcomes are claimed. All expected effects are stated as a priori hypotheses, with references to the original publications (Touvron et al., 2023, "LLaMA 2: Open Foundation and Fine-Tuned Chat Models"; Ashkboos et al., 2024, "QuaRot: Outlier-Free 4-Bit Inference in Rotated LLMs"). Quantitative figure sketches in tables are analytical lower-bound estimates produced with plain Python formulas, not measured throughput.

Notation follows the QuaRot paper: W4 / A4 are 4-bit weights / 4-bit activations; K4 / V4 are 4-bit elements of the KV-cache; per-channel refers to weight quantization along the output dimension of each Linear layer; per-token refers to activation quantization along the sequence dimension; fused RMSNorm + Hadamard refers to a single kernel that combines RMSNorm, an orthogonal Hadamard rotation, and per-token 4-bit quantization of the resulting hidden state.

## 1. Research Question and Hypotheses

RQ. How does QuaRot's end-to-end 4-bit quantization (W4A4 with K4V4 KV-cache, online dequant in fused RMSNorm+Hadamard+Linear) change the latency and throughput of the prefill and decoding phases of LLaMA-2 family models relative to an FP16 baseline, and how is the effect partitioned between rotation overhead, weight quantization, activation quantization, and KV-cache quantization?

A priori hypotheses (each tied to a source-supported mechanism; not outcomes):

H1 (prefill compute-bound). Prefill is matmul-bound on Linear layers; activation dequant can be hidden behind compute. Expected effect direction: small latency increase in W4A4 vs FP16, dominated by extra dequant instructions when the GEMM is well-utilized. Reference: roofline argument discussed in QuaRot, Section 4, and standard inference roofline for transformer decoders.

H2 (decoding memory-bound). Decoding is bandwidth-bound; per-token cost is roughly proportional to total weight bytes streamed. W4 reduces weight traffic by ~4x; K4V4 reduces KV traffic by ~4x. Quantitatively the memory floor drops by a factor that depends on the weight:activation:KV ratio, and so does the relative slowdown of W4A4 vs FP16. Reference: QuaRot, Section 4 (memory-bandwidth analysis); standard autoregressive inference analyses.

H3 (rotation overhead). Online Hadamard rotation and its fusion with RMSNorm should add a single-digit percent overhead when implemented as a fused kernel. This overhead is a confound that the design isolates with a dedicated control arm (QuaRot-W4A16: rotation + 4-bit weights + FP16 activations).

H4 (KV ablation). Keeping weights and activations at 4-bit while restoring KV-cache to FP16 (K4V16) is expected to remove the per-token KV memory traffic component while preserving all other dequant overheads. This isolates the unique contribution of 4-bit KV. The mirror arm (no rotation, naive W4A4 RTN, K4V4) isolates the standalone contribution of the Hadamard rotation to both speed and quality.

H5 (quality bound). Quality is expected to degrade within the limits reported in the QuaRot paper for LLaMA-2: a small WikiText-103 perplexity delta and a small zero-shot delta across HellaSwag, ARC-Challenge, WinoGrande, PIQA, BoolQ. Numerical success criteria are stated in Section 4; they are not predictions of our experiment.

H6 (GQA interaction, 70B-only). In LLaMA-2-70B, the KV-cache is shared across query head groups (GQA, 8 KV heads). K4V4 interacts with GQA differently than with classic MHA in 7B/13B: KV memory traffic is already smaller, so the marginal bandwidth saving from K4V4 is reduced. The 70B tier is included exactly to characterize this interaction and is non-blocking for the main analysis.

H7 (workload interaction). The size and sign of the W4A4 latency delta may depend on the workload cell. Prefill contrast between cells is expected to be driven by matmul shape (batch * sequence); decoding contrast is expected to be driven by the weight-to-KV bandwidth ratio, which depends on context length and batch size.

## 2. Models and Quantization Modes

### 2.1 Models

Core subset (mandatory for the main analysis):
- LLaMA-2-7B (MHA): hidden 4096, intermediate 11008, 32 layers, 32 heads, head dim 128, 32 KV heads, vocab 32000.
- LLaMA-2-13B (MHA): hidden 5120, intermediate 13824, 40 layers, 40 heads, head dim 128, 40 KV heads, vocab 32000.

Conditional third tier (optional, non-blocking):
- LLaMA-2-70B (GQA, 8 KV heads): hidden 8192, intermediate 28672, 80 layers, 64 heads, head dim 128, 8 KV heads, vocab 32000. Single precision: FP16 with tensor parallel TP=4 on A100-80GB.

Rationale for the subset:
- 7B and 13B share MHA across all layers, so the only varying axis is parameter count and depth. They fit on a single A100-80GB in FP16, which removes TP-overhead as a confounder.
- 70B is the only GQA model in the LLaMA-2 family. H6 above is the only motivation for the tier; it is reported separately and explicitly conditioned on the availability of a 4x A100-80GB node and enough wall-clock budget.

### 2.2 Quantization modes (arms)

| ID | Weights | Activations | KV-cache | Hadamard rotation | Role |
|----|---------|-------------|----------|-------------------|------|
| FP16 | FP16 | FP16 | FP16 | off | baseline |
| E2E-W4A4 | W4 (per-channel) | A4 (per-token) | K4V4 | on | main QuaRot end-to-end mode |
| E2E-W4A4-KV16 | W4 (per-channel) | A4 (per-token) | FP16 | on | isolates KV contribution |
| QuaRot-W4A16 | W4 (per-channel) | FP16 | FP16 | on | isolates rotation + weight-only cost |
| RTN-W4A4 | W4 (per-channel) | A4 (per-token) | K4V4 | off | isolates value of Hadamard rotation |

Notes:
- The "core" list above is intentionally compact; no additional KV sub-configurations are introduced beyond K4V4 and K4V16.
- "Rotation on" means the full QuaRot recipe (offline Hadamard fusion into Linear weights and into the K/V projections; online application on the residual stream after fused RMSNorm). See Section 6.
- All arms share identical random Hadamard matrices (seeded) so that the only varying factors are quantization policy and rotation policy.

### 2.3 Why each control arm is needed (controls list)

- FP16: reference for both latency/throughput and quality; provides the deltas.
- E2E-W4A4-KV16: jointly with E2E-W4A4, isolates the contribution of K4V4 specifically. Difference (E2E-W4A4 - E2E-W4A4-KV16) = KV 4-bit effect.
- QuaRot-W4A16: jointly with E2E-W4A4, isolates the contribution of 4-bit activations and online dequant. Difference (E2E-W4A4 - QuaRot-W4A16) = A4 + online dequant effect.
- RTN-W4A4: jointly with E2E-W4A4, isolates the value of the Hadamard rotation given the same numerical format. Difference (E2E-W4A4 - RTN-W4A4) = rotation-induced effect on accuracy and on the activation quantization kernel.
- The five-way design supports a clean 2x2x2 structure: rotation on/off x weight-only-vs-end-to-end x KV4 vs KV16, with FP16 as the degenerate corner.

## 3. Workloads

### 3.1 Prompt composition

70% synthetic uniform-token prefix + 30% held-out C4 real prompts.
- Synthetic component: tokens drawn uniformly from the LLaMA-2 BPE vocabulary, length matched per cell. Provides a stationary workload for steady-state prefill cost and clean batch-fill at decoding start.
- Real component: contiguous segments from a held-out C4 split, pre-tokenized with the LLaMA-2 BPE tokenizer, BOS-prefixed. Reproducibility: fixed random seed and fixed split index.

Rationale: the synthetic component removes confounds from natural-language statistics and lets batch-fill be exact for any batch size; the real component ensures that TTFT measurements reflect realistic prompt statistics and embedding outliers.

### 3.2 Prefill cells

Context lengths: {512, 1024, 2048, 4096} tokens. Max selected at the native LLaMA-2 context window (no RoPE-scaling). For each context length, batches are constructed by stacking right-padded prompts of equal length; no left-padding.

Outputs of prefill: the logits and the populated KV-cache (with the quantization policy of the current arm).

### 3.3 Decoding cells

Output lengths: {128, 512} tokens. Batch sizes: {1, 2, 8, 32, 64}. KV length at the start of decoding: matched to one of the prefill context lengths (512, 1024, 2048, 4096). Decoding uses greedy decoding (argmax) to remove sampling noise from the timing signal; a separate quality pass uses temperature sampling or nucleus if needed.

### 3.4 Workload cells (cartesian product)

For the core (7B, 13B) subset, the full grid is:
- Models: 2.
- Arms: 5.
- Prefill contexts: 4.
- Decoding outputs x batches x prefill KV-lengths: (2 outputs) x (5 batches) x (4 KV-lengths) = 40.
- Quality: per (model x arm) pair on WikiText-103 plus five zero-shot tasks.

For the conditional 70B tier: identical grid at TP=4.

## 4. Metrics and Success Criteria

### 4.1 Prefill metrics

- TTFT (Time-To-First-Token), milliseconds. Defined as elapsed GPU time from the first kernel launch of the prefill pass to the moment the first output token is sampled.
- Prefill throughput, tokens/s, summed across the batch. Reported as median and p50/p90/p99 across trials.
- Peak GPU memory, MB, captured with cuda allocator telemetry; activation memory is reported separately as the residual peak between the start of prefill and the end of prefill.
- Per-kernel timing breakdown, optional: GEMM time, RMSNorm+Hadamard+dequant time, attention time, gather/scatter time. Collected only for a small subset of cells to support the attribution in H3.

### 4.2 Decoding metrics

- Per-token latency, ms/token, mean and p50/p90/p99 over the generated sequence.
- End-to-end latency for fixed output length 128 and 512, ms per request.
- Throughput, tokens/s/GPU, computed at the batch level.
- KV-cache peak memory as a function of prefill KV-length; reported for both K4V4 and FP16 to make the KV-cache saving explicit.

### 4.3 Quality metrics

- Perplexity on the WikiText-103 standard split (raw), forward pass over the full text in evaluation stride. Reported as PPL and the delta vs FP16.
- Zero-shot accuracy on HellaSwag, ARC-Challenge, WinoGrande, PIQA, BoolQ, using log-likelihood ranking as in the LLaMA-2 paper (Touvron et al., 2023) and as in QuaRot (Ashkboos et al., 2024). Reported as accuracy and the delta vs FP16.

### 4.4 A priori success criteria

The study is considered consistent with the design hypotheses if and only if all of the following hold simultaneously (criteria, not predictions):
- Delta-perplexity on WikiText-103 standard split (QuaRot arm vs FP16) is bounded by +0.5 absolute.
- Mean delta across the five zero-shot tasks is bounded by +2.0 percentage points (positive direction: accuracy not worse).
- Multiple-comparison correction: Benjamini-Hochberg at q=0.05 across the five downstream tasks, applied per model.
- CI construction: 95% bootstrap CI over requests (not tokens, not batches) for every reported metric.

If any criterion fails, the affected arm is reported and excluded from the primary latency tables; the data are still reported for analysis.

## 5. Measurement Procedure and Statistical Plan

### 5.1 Timing instrumentation

- All timings use torch.cuda.Event with explicit synchronization between phases.
- Sampling window: after CUDA context warm-up, kernels are aligned to a fixed graph snapshot. Wall-clock is not the primary signal; CPU launch latency is excluded from TTFT.
- White-noise control: GPU clocks and memory clocks are locked via nvidia-smi -lgc; CUDA_DEVICE_MAX_CONNECTIONS=1; power limit recorded; ambient GPU temperature reported.

### 5.2 Trials and warm-up

- Per cell (defined by the cartesian product in Section 3.4), N = 50 measured trials.
- First 10 trials per cell are warm-up and are discarded before statistics; warm-up is used to stabilize allocator state, JIT cache state, and clock-domain negotiation.
- Each cell is rerun twice with a different RNG seed; pairs are compared for drift > 5% on the median metric; if drift exceeds 5%, the cell is rerun in a third pass and the median of three is reported.

### 5.3 Statistical reporting

- Latency metrics: median, IQR, p99, 95% bootstrap CI (10,000 resamples over trials).
- Throughput and memory: mean, std, 95% bootstrap CI.
- Quality metrics: point estimate on the full evaluation set; 95% bootstrap CI over evaluation prompts (per task).
- Multiple comparisons across downstream tasks: Benjamini-Hochberg at q=0.05.

### 5.4 Hardware configuration

- Primary class: NVIDIA A100-SXM4-80GB.
  - 7B and 13B: a single A100-80GB.
  - 70B (conditional): TP=4 across a 4x A100-80GB node.
  - Software stack: FP16 tensor cores; FP32 accumulator; H100 is *not* a target of the primary measurements.
- Secondary architecture (deferred, see feasibility): NVIDIA H100-SXM5-80GB. Not part of the core measurements; it is included only to discuss expected scaling in the feasibility section.

### 5.5 Illustrative magnitudes (analytical, not measured)

The table below is produced from open Python formulas (parameter counts encoded by hand, standard transformer formulas). It is included only to fix the orders of magnitude that motivate the workload grid; numbers are analytical, not measured.

| Model | Approx params (B) | KV cache at 4096 (FP16 / K4V4) | Forward prefill FLOPs at P=2048 (TFLOPs) | Forward prefill FLOPs at P=4096 (TFLOPs) |
|-------|-------------------|---------------------------------|------------------------------------------|------------------------------------------|
| LLaMA-2-7B  | ~6.5  | 64.0 MB / 16.0 MB     | 26.5  | 53.0  |
| LLaMA-2-13B | ~12.7 | 80.0 MB / 20.0 MB     | 52.0  | 103.9 |
| LLaMA-2-70B | ~68.5 | 16.0 MB / 4.0 MB (GQA)| 280.4 | 560.8 |

Approximate memory traffic lower bounds for one forward decoding token at context length 4096:

| Model | FP16 weights + FP16 KV (MB/token, lower bound) | W4 weights + K4V4 (MB/token, rough incl. block scales) |
|-------|--------------------------------------------------|--------------------------------------------------------|
| LLaMA-2-7B  | ~13019 | ~3660 |
| LLaMA-2-13B | ~25459 | ~7158 |
| LLaMA-2-70B | ~136919 | ~38508 |

These traffic numbers feed the roofline argument in Section 8.

## 6. QuaRot Implementation Details

The implementation follows the procedural recipe in Ashkboos et al., 2024, Section 3.

Step 1: Orthogonal Hadamard matrix H is constructed offline. The matrix is applied block-diagonally across head_dim-aligned tiles (block size 4 or full Fast Walsh-Hadamard) so that the per-block rotation can be fused into RMSNorm's output.

Step 2: For each Linear layer whose input is post-RMSNorm (Q/K/V/O projections and the MLP gate/up/down projections), the weight matrix is folded with H offline: W_A <- W_A * H. For the residual connection on the other side, the inverse rotation H^T = H^{-1} is applied online on the residual branch. FP-equivalence to the unrotated model is preserved exactly.

Step 3: RoPE is folded into the K and V projections so that the rotated KV-cache remains compatible with Q in the rotated space; this is the precondition for caching K and V in 4-bit form without an explicit online rotation.

Step 4: Weight quantization is performed offline using RTN (round-to-nearest) on a calibration set of 256 sequences drawn from C4 (held-out), per-channel symmetric 4-bit on each Linear layer.

Step 5: Activation quantization is performed online at runtime using a per-token symmetric 4-bit scheme. The dequantization is fused into the Linear matmul via a Triton or CUDA kernel that loads the packed int4 weights, broadcasts the per-channel scale, and applies the per-token scale on the activations in registers.

Step 6: RMSNorm is fused with the residual-stream Hadamard rotation and the online per-token dequant; output is block-wise quantized 4-bit with a per-block scale.

Step 7: KV-cache is quantized per-head with K4 / V4 symmetric, kept in a packed int4 buffer; on the attention path, K and V are dequantized on the fly for the QK^T and softmax*P passes.

Step 8: Sanity-check FP-equivalence. Before any timing collection, a deterministic pass is run on a 10-sequence subset of C4 through the rotated+quantized model and the FP16 reference. The maximum absolute logit difference and the maximum KL between output distributions are recorded; the kernel is signed off only if the logit difference stays within the empirical FP32-noise envelope observed across TT perturbation runs of the FP16 reference (no absolute number is enforced a priori).

## 7. Feasibility, Resource Envelope, and Threats to Validity

### 7.1 Feasibility

Experimental execution is explicitly out of scope for this design-only deliverable; no claims of execution are made here. The design below is sufficient to plan a run on bare metal or in a containerized environment.

Primary hardware: a single A100-SXM4-80GB is sufficient for 7B and 13B in any of the five arms. For 70B the conditional tier requires 4x A100-80GB with tensor parallel TP=4. The class is chosen because the QuaRot publication itself reports on A100-80GB, which removes vendor- and platform-level confounds when comparing reconstructed measurements to the public report.

Deferred secondary architecture: H100-SXM5-80GB. The H100 raises memory bandwidth and adds FP8 tensor cores; it is expected to shift the bandwidth-bound decoding ceiling upward in absolute tokens/s and to widen the gap between FP16 throughput and W4A4 throughput (because the bandwidth reduction from W4A4 still helps, but the absolute bandwidth ceiling is higher). This expectation is qualitative and is not part of the rubric of measured cells of this study; it is mentioned only to flag the natural follow-up.

Resource envelope (rough nominal estimate). Counts use the workload grid in Section 3.4:
- Core grid (7B + 13B): 2 models x 5 arms x 4 prefill contexts x (2 outputs x 5 batches x 4 KV-lengths) x 50 trials = 80,000 timing samples per metric, plus a one-time warm-up overhead along the same order. Aggregate order: tens of thousands of measured phases; on a single A100-80GB this maps to on the order of several days of wall-clock, plus the quality pass (PPL on WikiText-103 plus five zero-shot tasks per arm), which adds a single-digit fraction of that budget. The numbers are nominal; actual wall-clock depends on kernel maturity and the exact fused-kernel throughput.
- Conditional tier (70B, TP=4): same shape of grid; absolute phase count is the same, but per-phase cost grows with N and KV-length; expect an order-of-magnitude more wall-clock. Reported separately and non-blocking.

### 7.2 Threats to validity

1. Tensor-parallel overhead in the 70B tier. Collective operations (all-reduce / all-gather) add deterministic communication latency that is not a property of the quantization arm. Mitigation: report TP time separately and compare arms within TP=4 only; do not compare 70B-W4A4 against 7B/13B-W4A4 directly.

2. Fused-kernel maturity. The fused RMSNorm+Hadamard+Linear CUDA/Triton kernel is the dominant implementation-level confounder. A slow fused kernel can wash out the W4A4 speed-up at decoding; a fast fused kernel can amplify it. Mitigation: the QuaRot-W4A16 arm is the direct measurement of online dequant cost without activating A4; the sanity-check FP-equivalence pass in Section 6 validates kernel correctness at the FP level; any cell failing the sanity check is excluded.

3. Reference vs reimplementation drift. The QuaRot reference (Hugging Face + custom CUDA) and any Triton reimplementation may differ in scheduling, register pressure, and memory layout. Mitigation: report implementations used per arm; for the main analysis, prefer the QuaRot reference where available; for cross-implementation comparison, restrict attention to the relative delta between arms within the same implementation.

4. Calibration sensitivity. The 256 C4 calibration sequences used for offline weight quantization influence accuracy in a way that may interact with the rotation step. Mitigation: keep the calibration set fixed across arms that share the rotation matrix (i.e., across E2E-W4A4, E2E-W4A4-KV16, QuaRot-W4A16); report a sensitivity mini-sweep over calibration sequence count {64, 256, 1024} only as an appendix.

5. Workload-cell sensitivity. Relative deltas between arms may flip sign with context length and batch size (H7). Mitigation: the grid is a full cartesian product and is reported as a heat-map, not a single representative cell; the Analysis Plan in Section 8 foregrounds the (B, S) axis.

6. Confounders from kernel-vs-arithmetic. The asymmetry between compute throughput (FP16/INT8 tensor cores) and memory bandwidth on A100 means that some observed prefill deltas may come from lost tensor-core utilization for INT4 paths. Mitigation: report per-kernel FLOPs/byte ratio per cell using measured timings and analytical weight/activation counts, so the bottleneck classification in Section 8 is explicit per cell.

7. Quality regression correlated with mode. Failures of the success criteria in Section 4 would invalidate a latency claim based on the same arm. Mitigation: the design reports arms that fail the quality criteria in a separate excluded appendix and does not blend them into the main latency tables.

## 8. Analysis Plan

The analysis is split into two complementary subplans; each subplan reuses the same workload grid and metrics defined in Sections 3 and 4.

### 8.1 Prefill analysis

Dominant operation. At prefill, every Linear layer executes a GEMM of shape (B * S) x h_in x h_out. Roofline argument (analytical, per Section 5.5 table): for 7B and 13B, the FLOPs per byte ratio stays comfortably above the A100-80GB ridge point for any S in the grid, regardless of the arm. Expected classification: prefill is compute-bound across the core grid.

What the cells measure.
- (a) TTFT as a function of S, parameterized by arm, with B = 1 in the primary table and B in {2, 8, 32} in the secondary table. Hypothesis H1 predicts a small, positive, roughly arm-independent slope of TTFT vs S within each B; the E2E-W4A4 arm should be slightly above FP16 with a near-constant ratio.
- (b) Prefill throughput vs B at fixed S. Hypothesis H1 predicts that throughput scales almost linearly with B in FP16 up to HBM capacity, and similarly in W4A4 (since the compute-bound ridge is unaffected). If the W4A4 line shows a shallower slope at large B, the cause is most likely loss of tensor-core utilization for INT4 GEMM (Threat 6).
- (c) Activation memory peak vs S. W4A4 shortens activation footprints by ~4x relative to FP16; this should manifest as a roughly halved slope of peak-memory-vs-S in the W4A4 arms. This is a free, easy-to-verify side-effect of the design.

Attribution.
- Rotation overhead at prefill: difference (QuaRot-W4A16 - FP16) at matched (B, S).
- Activation dequant at prefill: difference (E2E-W4A4 - QuaRot-W4A16).
- KV 4-bit at prefill (KV population): difference (E2E-W4A4 - E2E-W4A4-KV16).
- Rotation value (with A4 active): difference (E2E-W4A4 - RTN-W4A4). Sign and magnitude depend on whether the rotation-enabled kernel is scheduler-friendly.

Quality pre-check before reporting prefill deltas: run the WikiText-103 PPL pass and the five zero-shot tasks for the E2E-W4A4 arm and the RTN-W4A4 arm; both must satisfy Section 4 success criteria for the prefill tables to include the full grid.

Conditional 70B tier (GQA). The prefill analysis is rerun with TP=4; expected scaling follows the same families, with an extra column reporting the TP communication fraction. Because 70B has fewer KV heads (8 vs 32 / 40), the K4V4 saving at prefill is smaller in absolute terms; this is reported as a per-cell ratio rather than as a delta in milliseconds.

### 8.2 Decoding analysis

Dominant operation. At decoding, every forward step reuses all weights and reads the full KV-cache of length S (or B*S with cross-batch sharing). Roofline (Section 5.5): per-token memory traffic is dominated by weights for S up to a few thousand, then transitions to KV-bound for very long S. Hypothesis H2 predicts that W4A4K4V4 reduces per-token traffic by a factor of about 3.5-4x in the small-S, large-B regimes and less in the long-S, small-B regime.

What the cells measure.
- (a) Per-token latency vs S, parameterized by arm, at fixed B. At B = 1 the per-token memory traffic scales linearly with S, so the W4A4K4V4 line should have a shallower slope than the FP16 line, with a near-constant vertical offset determined by the weight-read savings.
- (b) Per-token latency vs B, parameterized by arm, at fixed S. As B grows, weight traffic amortizes per request (not per token), so the latency-vs-B slope flattens for FP16; for W4A4K4V4 the slope is less steep because the starting weight traffic is already ~1/4.
- (c) Throughput vs B; the decoding throughput ceiling per GPU is bandwidth divided by per-token bytes; the upper-bound numbers implied by the Section 5.5 table define a trajectory that each arm's throughput should track at large B.
- (d) End-to-end latency at fixed output length 128 vs 512. Differences between arms in this metric combine a fixed startup cost (prefill, addressed in 8.1) with the per-token slopes above; reporting it isolates whether the per-token advantage dominates the total at long outputs.

Attribution. The attribution script mirrors Section 8.1:
- Weight-only W4 effect: (QuaRot-W4A16 - FP16); isolates the cost of 4-bit weights and online dequant in the absence of A4 (rotation present).
- A4 + online-dequant effect: (E2E-W4A4 - QuaRot-W4A16).
- K4V4 effect: (E2E-W4A4 - E2E-W4A4-KV16). For 7B/13B, where KV traffic is a meaningful fraction at long S, this is expected to be the largest per-cell difference in the W4A4 cell. For 70B, the same difference is expected to shrink by an order of magnitude or more because the K dimension is eight-fold smaller.
- Rotation value with A4 active: (E2E-W4A4 - RTN-W4A4). This single comparison carries both the speed and the accuracy benefit of QuaRot over a naive int-only quantization.

Quality pre-check before reporting decoding deltas: identical to Section 8.1, plus a paired comparison of E2E-W4A4-KV16 vs E2E-W4A4 to detect whether dropping KV4 (restoring FP16 KV) recovers quality; if so, the latency table explicitly flags the arm as a higher-quality mode.

Conditional 70B tier (GQA). GQA reduces KV bandwidth; the decoding analysis reuses the same plot axes. The expected signature is a smaller per-cell benefit of K4V4 vs 7B/13B and a smaller absolute KV share of per-token traffic. The 70B row in every decoding plot is therefore reported on its own axis or with a 70B-only inset, to keep the comparison with MHA models interpretable.

### 8.3 Joint prefill + decoding view

For each (model, arm) pair, a summary figure reports:
- TTFT vs S at B = 1.
- Per-token latency vs S at B = 1 and B = 64.
- Throughput at large B.
- KV-cache peak memory at S = 4096.
- PPL and zero-shot accuracy delta vs FP16.

The summary is repeated for 7B, 13B, and conditionally 70B; each block carries its own CI and a one-line classification (compute-bound vs bandwidth-bound) derived from the cell's empirical FLOPs/byte ratio. The figure is the unified reviewer-facing artifact of the eventual measurement phase; this design defines it but does not produce it.

---

End of design document. Implementation is not in scope; reviewers are invited to comment on the (a) workload grid, (b) the choice of K4V4 vs K4V16 as the single KV ablation, (c) the success criteria in Section 4, and (d) the threats listed in Section 7.2.
